branches.pr_title: fontforge: decode quoted glyph names; stop emitting aalt-only lookups as prefixes
branches.pr_body:
> **Note**: This post was generated by an AI agent (Claude) working under the guidance of
> @felipesanches, but submitted **without human review**. @felipesanches himself would
> still need to participate in the PR thread if he wants to contribute to the review.

Two fixes to the FontForge (.sfd) reader; no new flags.

- Quoted glyph names (always on): a quoted `StartChar:` name is FontForge's modified UTF-7, the encoding the reader already decodes for subtable, lookup, class and nameid strings. The name is now trimmed, unquoted and decoded, so `"C+AJIA-rculo0"` becomes `C`, U+0092, `rculo0` instead of keeping the `+` (and, with trailing whitespace, the closing quote).
- aalt-only lookups (always on): a lookup registered only to `aalt` is already inlined into the aalt feature, so it is no longer also emitted as a named feature prefix that nothing references. A lookup that a chain context calls by name keeps its definition.

Tests: 3 new unit tests in convertors/fontforge.rs. `cargo test -p babelfont`: 200 passed, 11 failed; upstream/main 6ab2312: 197 passed, the same 11 failed (the robocjk and decomposecomponentreferences tests that load the untracked noto-cjk-varco/notosanscjksc.rcjk fixture). Integration 7/7 and doc-tests 4/4 pass on both. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --all-targets` (also with `--features cli`): 0 warnings, as on main.

branches.pr_title: Add opt-in filters that keep what a FontForge source states
branches.pr_body:
> **Note**: This post was generated by an AI agent (Claude) working under the guidance of
> @felipesanches, but submitted **without human review**. @felipesanches himself would
> still need to participate in the PR thread if he wants to contribute to the review.

Five opt-in filters that keep what a FontForge source states, and what FontForge's own exporter wrote from it: codepoints, contour direction, glyph names, advances and component placement.

- `--drop-alternate-unicodes`: drop the plain AltUni2 alternate codepoints, which FontForge's TTF export did not emit. Variation sequences are untouched; a glyph is never left unmapped.
- `--reverse-path-direction`: reverse every closed contour; the counterpart to `--correct-path-direction` for a font whose mixed directions are meant to be kept.
- `--keep-source-glyph-names`: set the Glyphs custom parameter "Don't use Production Names" in the source; main.rs honours it when babelfont itself compiles.
- `--keep-source-advances`: record an uncategorised glyph with a non-zero advance as a base, so a GlyphData name lookup cannot zero it as a mark. Run `--infer-mark-category` first.
- `--snap-component-transforms`: read a component scale within 1.5 F2Dot14 steps of an integer as that integer (FontForge stores a mirror as -0.999939) and an offset within 0.1 unit as that unit, then round every offset with rint (ties to even), as `dumpcomposite()` in FontForge's tottf.c does.

They appear under two new --help headings, "Filters for reproducing a legacy FontForge export" and "Filters for keeping what the source states". The companion FontForge OS/2-defaults PR adds to the first one, so whichever of the two merges second needs a one-hunk rebase of filters/mod.rs.

Tests: 7 new unit tests. `cargo test -p babelfont`: 204 passed, 11 failed; upstream/main 6ab2312: 197 passed, the same 11 failed (the robocjk and decomposecomponentreferences tests that load the untracked noto-cjk-varco/notosanscjksc.rcjk fixture). Integration 7/7 and doc-tests 4/4 pass on both. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --all-targets` (also with `--features cli`): 0 warnings, as on main.

branches.pr_title: Add opt-in filters for the OS/2 and post values FontForge's exporter computes
branches.pr_body:
> **Note**: This post was generated by an AI agent (Claude) working under the guidance of
> @felipesanches, but submitted **without human review**. @felipesanches himself would
> still need to participate in the PR thread if he wants to contribute to the review.

Three opt-in filters that fill the OS/2 and post values FontForge's TTF exporter computes when a source does not state them. A value the source states is never overwritten.

- `--fontforge-underline-position`: FontForge's UnderlinePosition is the underline's centre, post.underlinePosition its top. Applies `dumppost()`'s rule through tag 20170731, position - thickness/2; FontForge reversed the sign in commit 9f667c9c (fontforge/fontforge#3389).
- `--fontforge-os2-defaults`: fills the sub/superscript and strikeout metrics (`SFDefaultOS2SubSuper`, tottf.c), PANOSE (`SFDefaultOS2Simple`, byte 2 from `OS2WeightCheck`), and the x-height and cap height (`SFStandardHeight`, splinefont.c).
- `--fontforge-height-glyph-count-mean`: the x-height and cap height as a FontForge built before 2012-05-14 (commit 4d34d21ef866) computed them, with the sum of the distinct round tops divided by the glyph count. Run it before `--fontforge-os2-defaults`.

Independent of #90. With #90, the underline, strikeout and sub/superscript values also reach a .glyphs output as the custom parameters compilers read. The companion FontForge source-fidelity PR adds to the same --help heading, so whichever of the two merges second needs a one-hunk rebase of filters/mod.rs.

Tests: 21 new unit tests. `cargo test -p babelfont`: 218 passed, 11 failed; upstream/main 6ab2312: 197 passed, the same 11 failed (the robocjk and decomposecomponentreferences tests that load the untracked noto-cjk-varco/notosanscjksc.rcjk fixture). Integration 7/7 and doc-tests 4/4 pass on both. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --all-targets` (also with `--features cli`): 0 warnings, as on main.

issues.what: The name is decoded as UTF-7 even when it is not quoted. FontForge's writer (sfd.cpp SFDDumpCharStartingMarker) writes any all-ASCII name raw and unquoted, `+` included. Its reader (SFDGetChar) calls SFDReadUTF7Str only when the name starts with `"`; otherwise it takes the token literally. With this branch, `StartChar: a+b` loads as `a`, a duplicate of the real glyph `a`, and `StartChar: a+-b` loads as `a+b`. Base kept both literal, so this is a regression. Verified with a scratch test that gets ["a","a+b","a"] where ["a+b","a+-b","a"] is expected. The code comment, the commit message and the PR body all say only a QUOTED name is decoded, so the text is also false against the code. issues.what: PANOSE does not follow FontForge's rule, and the rustdoc describes FontForge wrongly. In tottf.c OS2WeightCheck at tags 20141014 and 20170731 and at master, the branch is `strstrmatch(weight,"extra") || strstrmatch(weight,"light")` -> panose[2]=3. The later 'light -> 4' branch can never run, yet the rustdoc lists 'light 4'. 'semi'+'bold' gives 7, where the filter gives 8 for 'SemiBold'. SFDefaultOS2Info also runs OS2WeightCheck a second time on sf->fontname (the PostScript FontName), and that match overrides the Weight: one. It sets panose[0]=3 when FontName contains 'script' (and not 'sans', not monospace), sets panose[3] from condensed/narrow/expanded words in FontName (8/6/5/7), and sets panose[3]=9 when SFOneWidth says every glyph has one width. The filter hard-codes bytes 0 and 3. When Weight: is missing it falls back to the preferred subfamily name, which FontForge never reads. Probe with FontForge's rule computed by hand: Weight: Light, FontName ProbeScript-SemiBoldCondensed. The filter gives [2,0,4,3,...], FontForge 20170731 gives [3,0,7,6,...]. issues.fix: Port OS2WeightCheck exactly: medi 6; demi|halb|(semi&&bold) 7; bold|fett|gras 8; heavy 9; black 10; nord 11; thin 2; extra|light 3; otherwise leave the value. Apply it to postscript_weight_name first and then to font.names.postscript_name, starting from 5, and drop the preferred_subfamily_name fallback. Add byte 0 = 3 for a FontName containing 'script' (not 'sans', not monospace), byte 3 from the FontName width words, and 9 when all advances are equal. Fix the rustdoc list. Add tests: Light -> 3; Weight Regular + FontName Foo-SemiBold -> 7; FontName FooScript -> byte 0 = 3. issues.what: The sub/superscript x-offsets come from the unrounded y-offsets. FontForge computes `os2_supxoff = s*pfminfo->os2_supyoff` and `os2_subxoff = -s*pfminfo->os2_subyoff`, where those fields are int16_t (splinefont.h:1151-1152). So it multiplies by the y-offset already truncated, 983 and 286 at a 2048 em, not 983.04 and 286.72. The rustdoc even quotes that C. Probe: ascender 1638, descender -410, SFD ItalicAngle -20. The filter writes SubscriptXOffset 98, FontForge 97. The same kind of mismatch shows up at 11 integer angles from -1 to -30 at a 2048 em, 8 at 1024 and 9 at 4096; there are none at 1000 or 2000.
issues.fix: let subyoff = (0.14 * em_f) as i32; let supyoff = (0.48 * em_f) as i32; return them for the Y offsets, and use (-s * f64::from(subyoff)) as i32 and (s * f64::from(supyoff)) as i32 for the X offsets. Add a test: 1638/-410 with internal angle +20 gives SubscriptXOffset 97 and SuperscriptXOffset -336. Mirror on gf-sfd-conversion.

issues.what: This block is not opt-in. It checks only whether the key com.schriftgestalt.Glyphs.customParameters.Don't use Production Names is present, and ignores its value and its disabled flag. So any .glyphs input that carries the parameter now compiles without production names, even when the source says value = 0 or disabled = 1. Confirmed with the built binary: .glyphs files with value=0 and with disabled=1 both compiled to a .ttf whose glyph order keeps 'mu' instead of 'uni03BC'. Base has no such code, so this is also an unannounced behaviour change for existing .glyphs-to-binary users.
issues.fix: Honour the parameter only when it is enabled and truthy. Reuse the {value, disabled} logic in glyphs3::customparameters::enabled_cp_value, e.g. `.get(KEY).and_then(|v| v.as_object()).is_some_and(|o| !o.get("disabled").and_then(|d| d.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false) && o.get("value").is_some_and(|v| v.as_i64() == Some(1) || v.as_bool() == Some(true)))`. issues.where: babelfont/src/filters/dropalternateunicodes.rs:13-14 and help :88-90; commit 32597d0 message; PR body bullet --drop-alternate-unicodes
issues.what: The premise 'FontForge's own TTF export did not emit those alternates' is conditional. In FontForge 20120731's tottf.c (format-4 cmap, ~lines 4520-4536; copy at ~/compartilhado/.claude/jobs/95a57d25/tmp/tottf.c), the cmap is built from the encoding map only when the font's encoding is UnicodeBmp/UnicodeFull. For every other encoding, the same function adds each plain BMP AltUni entry (vs==-1) to the cmap. The filter drops the alternates unconditionally, so for a Custom- or ISO-8859-1-encoded SFD it removes cmap entries that FontForge did emit.
issues.fix: The reader already stores the font encoding in font.format_specific["Encoding"]. Either gate the filter on UnicodeBmp/UnicodeFull and log a skip otherwise, or scope the rustdoc, the help, the 32597d0 message and the PR bullet to 'a Unicode-encoded SFD'. A code change must also go into gf-sfd-conversion, and the re-landed conversions built with it need re-checking.

issues.what: The rationale is wrong. It says '-0.999939 is exactly one F2Dot14 step from -1: it is a scale of -1 that has been through TrueType's component grid and back'. But F2Dot14 represents -1 exactly (0xC000), so a -1 cannot come back as -0.999939. -0.999939 is -16383/16384 rounded to six digits, and it is not exactly one step away (6.10e-5 vs 6.1035e-5). FontForge writes it as -1 only because put2d14 (tottf.c:598) floors onto the grid. That same floor writes +0.999939 as 16383/16384, whereas this filter snaps it to 1, so the scale rule is not the exporter's rule. Simon knows F2Dot14 and will catch this.
issues.fix: Reword along these lines: '-0.999939 is -16383/16384 written to six digits; FontForge's exporter floors a scale onto the F2Dot14 grid (put2d14 in tottf.c), which lands this value on -1. The snap reads a scale within 1.5 steps of an integer as that integer; it is not put2d14's rule (0.999939 is exported as 16383/16384).' Adjust the constant's doc and the test comment to match.
